memory_update.text: TYL should be retained as the reference benchmark for public-sector software modernization, but not treated as the main underfollowed alpha target because it is already a large-cap category leader.
IIIV is a promising underfollowed public-sector software candidate because it sits in courts, JusticeTech, public administration, and integrated payments with a small-cap market value.
TLS is a focused underfollowed candidate for FedRAMP/RMF/cyber compliance workflow bottlenecks; verify whether Xacta authorization converts into measurable SaaS growth.

SSTI is a speculative shadow candidate below the preferred market-cap range; include only if the research track explicitly tolerates controversial public-safety software exposure and validates contract durability.

For this node, procurement access, FedRAMP/RMF authorization, public-sector workflow specialization, court/public-safety data, and installed agency relationships appear to be more relevant chokepoints than generic AI software capability.

Need a follow-up pass on identity verification and government customer onboarding vendors; this pass found stronger evidence for public-sector workflow software and cyber compliance than for pure identity-verification exposure.

summary: Expanded the universe around government software modernization with a two-lane funnel. Tyler Technologies is the reference public-sector software anchor, while i3 Verticals, Telos, and SoundThinking represent underfollowed or speculative smaller-cap exposures to courts/public administration software, FedRAMP/RMF cyber compliance, and public-safety data workflows. The main chokepoint hypothesis remains that procurement access, domain-specific workflows, security accreditation, and installed public-sector relationships may matter more than generic AI/software capability.
